learning_outcomes.text: The student knows strategies for solving problematic situations.
The student understands the basics of motivational and emotional processes.
The student understands the need to build effective communication and cope with aggression.
The student can function in a group and assume various roles within it.

syllabus_topics: Basics of psychology: Introduction to general psychology, covering perception, thinking processes, emotions, motivation, and personality. Selected elements of social psychology relevant to the students' education profile.
Basic currents in contemporary psychology (Gestalt psychology, psychoanalysis, behaviorism, cognitive psychology).
Perceptual processes (role and types of receptors, factors determining perception processes).
Thinking (main types of thinking processes, strategies for solving problematic situations, obstacles in thinking processes, creativity, intelligence – concept, measurement, types of intelligence).
Human needs system (concept of need, selected concepts of human needs catalog, influence of need deprivation on human functioning).
Emotions (activation and its influence on task effectiveness, types of emotions, feelings and dynamics of feelings).
Motivation (concept of motivation and motivational process – directing, mobilizing, and organizing function; drive motivational mechanism, developmental motivational mechanism).
Aggression and aggressiveness (concept, causes and types of aggression; influence of aggression on functioning effectiveness, ways to reduce aggressive tendencies).
Conformity and group influence (concept and essence of conformity, types of conformist mechanisms, factors determining the level of conformity).
Interpersonal communication (concept of communication, elements of communication process, selected communication concepts, factors disrupting effective communication).
assessment_rules: Learning outcomes are verified by completing the classes. For lectures, verification methods include activity during classes and a test. Student presence at lectures is expected, with students asking questions and clarifying doubts. Audiovisual recording of lectures requires the instructor's consent.
